# git proxy

Replace the alias-based extension of git with a proxy binary: the shell would alias `git` to a wrapper (`tig` in the sketch), and the wrapper would implement the author's extra commands itself while forwarding everything else to the real `git`.

```bash
alias git="tig"
```

```bash
$ git state
> git state -> tig state -> cobra state command
$ git status
> git status -> git status
```

The argument: the extra commands are extensions, not aliases, and belong in a real program with subcommands (Cobra-style), help and tests; a proxy also lifts the restrictions of git aliases (no aliases of aliases, no shell functions). The one hazard named is recursion — the proxy must call the real binary by path, not through the alias.
